clue.text: Perhaps who's cured individuals' breaks?

indicators.note: breaks here means one word splits the other open and sits inside it

parts.note: someone cured is better again
individuals are ones, single units

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who it is that mends people's fractures.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: ONES breaks into BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonesetter is a traditional practitioner who resets fractured or dislocated limbs, curing people's breaks.

clue.text: Stay in vehicle number eleven

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
K is the eleventh letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone told to remain sitting on the number 11 bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a stiffening strip in a corset, called a busk.
explanation.definitionFit: A busk is a stiffening strip of whalebone or steel in a corset, a kind of stay.

clue.text: Anorak held by dinner date

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words dinner date, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A geeky person being taken out to dinner on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, much like a geek.

clue.text: What compels one, flying kite

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered in the air and landing in a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Asking what drives someone to fly a kite.
explanation.walkthrough: Kite is old RAF slang for an aeroplane; the Sopwith Camel was a First World War fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: In airmen's slang a kite is any aircraft, and the Sopwith Camel is a famous biplane fighter.

clue.text: Tension initially dropping in part of Barnet

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for tension is dropped

parts.note: tension is stress

explanation.surface: Stress easing somewhere in Barnet, a borough of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), not the London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock of hair, and Barnet means hair in rhyming slang.

clue.text: With special sense, muse about new language

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a special sixth sense

indicators.note: about means the muse's name goes around the letter for new

parts.note: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric poetry

explanation.surface: A poet with intuition musing over a freshly invented tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is a constructed international language devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: One's composed poetic address to Manx cat?

parts.note: O is the poetic vocative, as in 'O Muse'

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Someone composing a poem addressed to a tailless Manx cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical work, something a composer has written.

clue.text: Men backing film put in cash to make capital

indicators.note: put in means the pieces go inside the word for cash

parts.note: pence is small cash

indicators.note: backing means the soldiers' abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers or men
vid is short for video, a film

explanation.surface: Investors backing a film to make a financial profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, but it is a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the capital city of the US state of Rhode Island.

clue.text: Sweet stuff from bee, say, covering rough gem

indicators.note: covering means the bee word wraps around the jumbled gem

parts.note: a bee is an example of a stinger

indicators.note: rough signals the letters of gem are put in disorder

explanation.surface: Honey from a bee coating an uncut gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is the tender ginger root preserved in syrup, a sweet confection.

clue.text: Way to make shape, perhaps, getting tips

indicators.note: way to make tells us the answer is a recipe that would produce the following word

parts.note: shape is one of the words an anagram of a five-letter word for piles can make

explanation.surface: Advice on how to get into shape, with handy hints.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: SCRAP HEAPS means jumble HEAPS, and one result is SHAPE. 'tips' looks like hints, but it is British for rubbish dumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a tip is a rubbish dump, and scrapheaps are piles of discarded junk.

clue.text: One poet or another keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the other poet holds the quiet letter inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe is another poet
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Two poets, one of them staying silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century English poet, author of The Rape of the Lock.

clue.text: Give orders about every drink of spirits

parts.note: C is circa, about
every shot of liquor is all the shots

explanation.surface: A boss ordering a round of spirits for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To call the shots is an idiom meaning to be in charge and make the decisions.

clue.text: Bill's introduction, stepping on more than one tree

indicators.note: on means the stepping word is placed after the trees

parts.note: firs are trees, plural
stepping is treading

explanation.surface: Someone walking over the roots of several trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is a parliamentary bill, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reading is the formal introduction of a parliamentary bill to the legislature.

clue.text: New iPod — it gets cover impossible to mess up

indicators.note: new signals the letters given are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: a roof is a cover

explanation.surface: A new iPod comes with a protective case that can't be damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idiot-proof is so simple that even a fool cannot operate it wrongly.

clue.text: Winning cheers up soldiers obstructing corruption

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for cheers is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British for thanks, cheers

indicators.note: obstructing means the soldiers block the middle of the corruption word

parts.note: taint is corruption
men are soldiers

explanation.surface: Cheering soldiers trying to stop corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainment, like winning, is the achieving or gaining of something sought.

clue.text: Rustic building's other half has right chopping block

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife, one's other half

indicators.note: chopping means the letter for right cuts into the block word

parts.note: to ban is to block
R is right

explanation.surface: Someone's partner using a chopping block in a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch for wife comes from Cockney rhyming slang (Duchess of Fife).
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is a farm structure with a roof but open sides, used for storing hay.

clue.text: Item used when flying bird breaks switch

indicators.note: breaks means the bird word splits the switch word open

parts.note: to switch is to alter
doing bird is British slang for doing time in prison

explanation.surface: A flying bird hits a switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is not a feather-bearing creature but slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is an instrument in an aircraft that measures height above the ground.

clue.text: Lawyer's right to welcome one extended rest

indicators.note: to welcome means the lawyer's word takes in the letter for one

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lawyer entitled to welcome a client before taking a long break.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a stay in bed later than usual, a lengthy morning rest.

clue.text: Sailor also called for port

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor
aka is also known as

explanation.surface: A sailor with a nickname heading for a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese seaport and city on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Shoo the cat away — no small trouble for canine?

indicators.note: away suggests the letters are sent off and scattered into a new order
no means the shoo word goes without the small letter

explanation.surface: Chasing off a cat, perhaps a cause of trouble for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a dog, but it is a canine tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is a pointed tooth, so a pain in one is toothache.

clue.text: With ire, guy is interrupting leader's unionist idea

indicators.note: interrupting means these pieces break into the leader's abbreviation

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, is a national leader
ire is anger
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: An angry man heckling the Prime Minister's political scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan-Germanism is the political ideology of uniting all German-speaking peoples in one state.

clue.text: Famous books in revolutionary study

indicators.note: in means the books sit inside the reversed study
revolutionary means the word for study is turned round

parts.note: a den is a study
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Well-known books on revolution found in a study.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known and celebrated, much as famous does.

clue.text: This person, getting cloned, is an internet hit

parts.note: this person is me, the speaker
being cloned makes an identical copy, so me again

explanation.surface: Someone who has been cloned going viral online.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an image or idea that spreads rapidly and popularly online.

clue.text: Case of cruelty — way medic may treat one

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A cruelty case, and the way a doctor might handle a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac of fluid that a doctor may drain or remove.

clue.text: Outstanding verse in recital

indicators.note: in recital means the word for verse is spoken aloud

parts.note: an ode is a poem, verse

explanation.surface: A superb poem performed at a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Outstanding in the sense of unpaid: a debt still owed.

clue.text: Where to find train lines carrying eastern rulers, say

indicators.note: carrying means the combined words hold the letter for eastern

parts.note: a train is found at a station
RY is railway, lines
E is eastern

explanation.surface: A train station whose lines carry Eastern monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rulers' looks like monarchs, but it is measuring sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulers are writing supplies, an example of stationery like pens and paper.

clue.text: Celebrate what will be announced

indicators.note: announced means the word for destiny is said aloud

parts.note: fate is what will be, destiny

explanation.surface: Celebrate whatever news is about to be announced.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them with festivities, to celebrate them.

clue.text: Colourful, free cutting that is with bouquet

indicators.note: cutting means the free word cuts into the that-is abbreviation

parts.note: ie is id est, that is
to rid is to free
a bouquet is a wine's scent

explanation.surface: A colourful, freshly cut bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like flowers, but it is the aroma of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent describes shimmering rainbow colours that shift with the angle of view.
